operations.label: RNA fragmentation (unlabelled interface)
operations.description: Whole-genome RNA supplies short linear RNA fragments before the drawn circularization.

evidence.locator: CirSeq row: Whole-genome RNA and adjacent purple linear RNA
CirSeq heading and first workflow paragraph
evidence.quote:
First, single-stranded RNAs are fragmented using Zn2+ and size-selected to no more than one-third of the sequencing read length.
Next, they are circularized and reverse-transcribed using random primers. Rolling-circle RT is used to generate tandem-repeat
cDNA strands.

operations.label: Circularize RNA with kinase and RNA ligase 1
operations.description: Linear RNA fragments become circular RNA templates.

evidence.locator: CirSeq row: Circularize RNA with kinase and RNA ligase 1; Circular RNA template

operations.label: Random primers
operations.description: Random-primed rolling-circle reverse transcription produces tandem-repeat cDNA from each circular RNA template.

evidence.locator: CirSeq row: Random primers; circular template with Repeat 1, Repeat 2 and Repeat 3

evidence.quote: The foundation of this approach is the circularization of fragmented viral RNAs, which are then redundantly encoded into tandem repeats by ‘rolling-circle’ reverse transcription. When sequenced, the redundant copies within each read are aligned to derive a consensus sequence of their initial RNA template.

operations.label: Repeat 1 / Repeat 2 / Repeat 3
operations.description: The cDNA readout yields repeated copies that are aligned for comparison; internal library preparation is not decomposed.

operations.label: Corrected sequence
